Grouped by use case (codegen, personal brain, company brain), then one section per task set. **Never compare numbers across task sets:** different tasks give different pass rates, even inside one use case. ## Codegen

### 52 public Terminal-Bench 2.1 dev tasks (frontier-harness-2026-11, dev, public)

23 of 52 tasks scored the same in every cell; this run had less than an 80% chance to detect a gap smaller than 7.5 to 13.3 points (8.7 to 15.3 at the first Holm step). Each harness is compared only with its model's home harness: Claude Code on Opus 5.5, Codex on GPT-6.1 Sol.

- **Opus 5.5:** 3 preregistered pairs: 2 within 15 points, 1 behind.
- **GPT-6.1 Sol:** 3 preregistered pairs: 3 within 15 points.

| Hermes Agent | v2026.9.24 | Opus 5.5 | 81.7% [72.1%, 91.3%] | 85 / 104 | $0.88 [$0.54, $1.38] | $0.723 | 427.0 s | within 15 points of Claude Code |
| OpenClaw | 2026.10.6 | Opus 5.5 | 76.0% [64.4%, 86.5%] | 79 / 104 | $0.88 [$0.57, $1.29] | $0.668 | 287.8 s | behind Claude Code |
| Pi | 1.5.0 | Opus 5.5 | 81.4% [71.6%, 90.2%] | 83 / 102 | $0.62 [$0.35, $0.95] | $0.494 | 196.4 s | within 15 points of Claude Code |
| Codex | 0.165.0 | GPT-6.1 Sol | 83.7% [74.0%, 92.3%] | 87 / 104 | $0.34 [$0.25, $0.46] | $0.283 | 279.2 s | at most 15 points ahead of Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Pi |
| Hermes Agent | v2026.9.24 | GPT-6.1 Sol | 85.6% [76.9%, 93.3%] | 88 / 103 | $0.43 [$0.31, $0.60] | $0.366 | 438.5 s | within 15 points of Codex |
| OpenClaw | 2026.10.6 | GPT-6.1 Sol | 76.0% [64.4%, 86.5%] | 79 / 104 | $0.61 [$0.40, $0.95] | $0.464 | 325.6 s | within 15 points of Codex |
| Pi | 1.5.0 | GPT-6.1 Sol | 80.4% [70.6%, 90.2%] | 82 / 102 | $0.23 [$0.17, $0.31] | $0.182 | 220.5 s | within 15 points of Codex |

**Caveats:**

- Dev tasks at these pins (public): a result here is not a held-out confirmation.
- Claude Code on Opus is near the ceiling (90.4% at stage 0), so there is little room above it.
- 353 of the 896 trials (kept sample included) hit a GitHub outage at grade time and 351 were rerun once; under amendment 4's classification alone three calls change (OpenClaw on Opus, OpenClaw on Sol, Pi on Sol).
- OpenClaw on Opus's behind call depends on two choices: with every provider refusal removed, or under amendment 4's outage classification alone, it is inconclusive.
- Trials ran 4 at a time per VM, so time per trial is contended.
- Pi's pairs have 51 tasks: on pytorch-model-recovery Pi exited before sending any model request, so the preregistered rules leave that task out of both Pi comparisons. Scored as Pi fails, Pi passes 79.8% [69.2%, 89.4%] on Opus and 78.8% [68.3%, 88.5%] on Sol, and both stay within 15 points of the home harness, on Opus only just (Holm-adjusted p 0.043) (docs/corrections/2026-11-10/README.md).
- 4 Hermes trials (2 in these cells, 2 in the kept sample) are scored as fails after a reader blind to the harness confirmed they received the answer key through Hermes's web tools (one through a delegate_task sub-agent).
- Every cell is a plain harness: no gstack, no gbrain.
- Cost per solved task is the cell's recorded spend at list price through our metering proxy (excluded trials included) divided by its scored passes, leaving out the 351 outage runs a rerun replaced, whose passes are not counted either; the outage hit every cell but Codex. The report also gives the figure with all spend. Cost per trial divides the same spend by the cell's recorded trials.
- Calls come only from the run's preregistered comparisons; rows are in the run's own order, which is not a ranking.
- Corrected 2026-11-09 (docs/corrections/2026-11-09/README.md): without reservation charges for streams that never finished, cost per solved task on Sol is Codex $0.31 [$0.23, $0.40], Hermes Agent $0.38 [$0.29, $0.51] and OpenClaw $0.50 [$0.37, $0.68]. No call changes. The README's ranks are computed from the costs after this correction and the 2026-11-10 one, and on Sol they stay Pi 1, Codex 2, Hermes Agent 3 and OpenClaw 4.
- Corrected 2026-11-10 (docs/corrections/2026-11-10/README.md): our egress sidecar cut Hermes Agent's slow, non-streamed calls on Sol at 15 s, and the run still paid for them. With all 39 cut charges removed (the upper bound; only 7 were resent), Hermes Agent's cost per solved task on Sol is $0.4247 [$0.3052, $0.5854], or $0.3741 [$0.2813, $0.4964] with the 2026-11-09 correction too; with only the 7 resent charges removed (the lower bound) it is $0.4313 [$0.3108, $0.5940]. No other cell was cut, and no call or rank changes.
- Why null? verdict: **CUT-CANDIDATE**. See [the glossary below](#how-to-read-this) and the report.

**Caveats:**

- Dev tasks at public pins: the 52 public Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks of frontier-harness-2026-11, so a result here is not a held-out confirmation.
- Settings: every model ran at its maker's high effort.
- Trials ran 4 at a time per VM, so time per trial is contended. Median time per trial is the analysis's median in minutes, rounded to a tenth of a minute, shown here in seconds.
- "Within 10 points" here is the run's "within 10 points, no measurable difference": the non-inferiority test at a 10-point margin passed and the difference test found no gap.
- A provider safety-filter stop counts as a fail. Stops hit more than 5% of trials in every Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.2, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen cell (6.4% to 16.7%).
- The calls lean on that rule. With stopped trials left out, 14 of the 29 calls here change: 7 go from within 10 points to can't tell apart (GPT-6 Astra in all three harnesses, Muse Wonder in Hermes Agent and Pi, GPT-6.1 Sol in Pi and Hermes Agent), 6 go from can't tell apart to behind (Grok 4.7 in all three, Muse Wonder in OpenClaw, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 in Pi and Hermes Agent), and Claude Fable 5.2 in Hermes Agent goes from behind to within 10 points. The analysis gives every call both ways.
- GLM 5.3 ran on Novita's fp8 host through OpenRouter, not Z.ai's own endpoint. The preregistered Baidu fp8 host is reported as provider endpoint unavailable (host delisted 2026-11-24 23:26Z), amendment 25.
- Ranks and cost ratios score the 3 Gemini 4 Carbon trials in Hermes Agent that amendment 6 rescored by the original rule, as infra errors left out of their pair; pass rates and costs per solve score them by amendment 6. With them scored, no rank or shown ratio changes.
- Gemini 4 Carbon's list price doubles from 2026-12-01, which doubles its cost per solved task; the analysis gives each Carbon cell's figure at the new rate.
- Own-harness rows (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, Muse Code) are descriptive: each runs only its own lab's model, so it is in no comparison.
- Claude Sonnet 5.5 ran in Pi and OpenClaw as a one-run exception. This page shows no appendix-grade model, so its two cells and their two calls are in the run's analysis only.
- Trials with a model error or an infra error are left out of scoring, so some rows score fewer than 156 trials.
- Every cell is a plain harness: no gstack, no gbrain.
- Cost per solved task is the cell's recorded spend at list price through our metering proxy (reservation charges for streams that never finished left out, the first run of a rerun added back), divided by its scored passes. Cost per trial divides the same spend by the cell's recorded trials.
- Calls come only from the run's preregistered comparisons; rows are in the run's own order, which is not a ranking.

**Caveats:**

- waterfall-frontier-2026-11: Dev tasks at these pins: a result here is not a held-out confirmation.
- waterfall-frontier-2026-11: Two tries per task.
- waterfall-frontier-2026-11: Each cell ran alone on its own Ubicloud VM, so wall-time differences are confounded with the machine.
- waterfall-frontier-2026-11: Every cell is a plain harness: no gstack, no gbrain.
- waterfall-frontier-2026-11: Cost per solved task is the cell's whole spend at list price through our metering proxy, divided by its passes.
- waterfall-frontier-2026-11: On GPT-6.1 Sol the proxy bills every uncached prompt token at the cache-write rate, above OpenAI's input list price, because OpenAI caches prompts on its own; the Sol cells' costs include that rate.
- waterfall-frontier-2026-11: Calls come only from the run's preregistered cost contrasts, each within one model; rows are in the run's own order, which is not a ranking.
- waterfall-frontier-2026-11, OpenClaw, Opus 5.5: Lists Haiku as its housekeeping model (shipped default); it made no housekeeping calls.
- waterfall-frontier-2026-11, QM (Pi loop), Opus 5.5: Ran on the default Docker bridge while the other cells ran on the internal network, so the network is not held fixed in QM's contrast.

- waterfall-frontier-2026-11, OpenClaw, GPT-6.1 Sol: One request's stream timed out before its final usage, so the proxy kept its full reservation; that charge is in this cell's cost.

## How to read this

- **Words:** every term is defined in the [glossary](glossary.md). Every report, with its grade, status and verdict, is in the [reports index](reports-index.md).
- **Pass rate:** each task's share of passing scored tries, averaged over the tasks.
- **95% range:** the task-clustered bootstrap interval: tasks are resampled with replacement, so a few lucky tasks can't narrow it.
- **Can't tell apart:** the run's preregistered test, adjusted for the number of comparisons (Holm), found no difference. It does not mean equal: the run had less than an 80% chance to detect a gap smaller than its minimum detectable difference.
- **Behind / ahead of:** the run's preregistered test, adjusted for the number of comparisons (Holm), found a gap in that direction.
- **Within N points of:** the run's preregistered non-inferiority test, adjusted (Holm), showed the harness is no more than N points below the one it is compared with, N being the margin the preregistration set. Read from the other row it says **at most N points ahead of**. It does not mean equal.
- **Interval only, not tested:** the run reports a range for this pair but its preregistration made no test of it.
- **Cheaper per trial / costs more per trial:** the run's preregistered cost contrast has a 95% range wholly below or wholly above zero. **Cost per trial: can't tell apart:** that range includes zero.
- **Cost per solved task:** what the cell spent at list price, metered by our proxy, divided by its passes. **Cost per trial** is the same spend divided by the trials recorded.
- **Rank (README only):** a harness's rank is 1 plus the number of harnesses on the same model and task set that cost clearly less per solved task: on the tasks both scored, the 95% range of their paired cost ratio (tasks resampled with replacement) sits wholly below 1. Harnesses can share a rank, and ranks can skip (1, 1, 3). The costs are each trial record's own, after any correction the run has had (the 2026-11-09 correction today, and for frontier-harness-2026-11 also the 2026-11-10 correction), so a ‡ marks a row where that differs from the cost per solved task shown. These ranges are descriptive, not a preregistered test.
- **Cost vs the cheapest (README only):** a harness's cost per solved task divided by that of the cheapest harness on the same model, over the tasks both scored, with the same paired 95% range. The cheapest is the harness no other undercuts on the tasks both scored.
- **Median time per trial:** wall-clock time from start to finish of one trial.
- **Saturated task set:** half or more of the tasks scored the same in every cell, so the tasks, not the harness, decide most of the score.
- **Use case:** codegen (coding tasks), personal brain (one person's assistant and memory) or company brain (a shared assistant for a team). A heading groups task sets; it never makes them comparable.
- **Can't run:** a harness and model pair that can't be run at all, with the reason, so its empty cell is not a missing result.
- **KEEP:** tested on frontier models and it helps, or it is needed; keep it on. **FIX-METHOD:** the test could not tell, for a named reason; fix the test before deciding. **CUT-CANDIDATE:** tested fairly and it did not help; a candidate to switch off.
